summary: A brick tower on a low sandy spit at Hansville, lit in 1880 for the entrance to Puget Sound; now a Kitsap County park with weekend tours and a Lighthouse Society rental.

access.note: Grounds open daily in daylight; lighthouse tours Saturdays and Sundays noon to 4 p.m., April to September (2026 season ended); lantern room not part of the tour; keeper dwelling is a vacation rental.

stay.note: Half of the keeper duplex is a U.S. Lighthouse Society vacation rental.

notes_for_editor: Sources disagree and the story says so: appropriation (1873 vs 1877), land (10 acres $1,000 March 1879 vs 40 acres $1,800 April 1879), tower height (10 or 11 ft square; 28.5 or 30 ft), date of the fourth-order lens (1898 per HistoryLink and the nomination vs 1915 per Lighthouse Friends; the USLHS place record lists a fourth-order original lens, against both detailed histories saying fifth-order), cause of the cracked lens (lightning 20 May 1930 per the Lighthouse Service Bulletin vs vapor explosion 1931 per HistoryLink), the Admiral Sampson death toll (11 first day vs 16), when Cary left (1937 vs 1939) and Scannell started (1888 vs 1889). Lighthouse Friends and HistoryLink are secondary and unreferenced in places; Maggs log is quoted second-hand through Lighthouse Friends. The 1917 Bulletin efficiency-flag table was read by line (Point No Point beside William H. Cary); its OCR table is messy, so the checker should view the page image. The 1891 storm entry is in the fiscal 1891 report page (header 1891) and the OCR is badly garbled; the bound volume holds more than one year. The 1878 Osmyn/Aureola sentence follows the nomination, whose grammar leaves unclear which vessel sank. Roster is the USLHS archive list (Kraig Anderson inventory), not confirmed in primary registers; USCG-era names are not in the prose. The Seattle Star said 6:05 a.m.; another listing gives 5:46. Venue facts (tours, roof project) were checked 2026-10-22 on the Friends site. Newspapers searched 1879-1882 found only an OCR-garbled 1880 Argus item about a Senate committee striking an appropriation for light and fog signals here; not used. Checker 2026-10-22: 1917 efficiency-flag line (Cary beside Point No Point) re-read in the PDF text; the flag was for fiscal 1916. The 1930 Bulletin says the lightning did no damage to the lens; HistoryLink's 1931 cracked-lens account is treated as a separate claim. Bell winding interval differs: 45 minutes (HistoryLink) vs 2.5 hours (Lighthouse Friends).
